title: Slide a turner under an egg patty inside a 65 mm deep tray, set it on a muffin, and re-cover the tray
instruction: Take the cover off the egg tray, put one egg on the muffin with the turner, and put the cover back on the tray.
context: Lifting a cooked egg patty onto a muffin with a turner is the familiar step at the heart of an egg breakfast sandwich, the top food at US fast-food breakfast: 37% of all such orders in August 2022 included one (Circana), and Americans spent more than $2.4 billion on breakfast sandwiches in the year to September 2023 (NielsenIQ). Kitchens keep cooked patties in a covered 1/3-size pan so that they stay moist, so the cover comes off for each patty and goes back on. The hard part is inside the pan: its walls draw in to a 267 x 121 mm floor, and two 89 mm patties leave 68 mm of flat floor at its near end, so the 127 mm blade must come in over the 65 mm wall tipped about 42 degrees, tip down at the patty's edge, and flatten as it slides under, then carry the 42.5 g patty about 32 cm and set it within 12 mm of the heel's centre, while the 0.22 kg cover is held clear or set aside off the pan, to be seated again at the end.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the counter top. (1) A 1/3-size polycarbonate food pan, 325 x 176 mm at the rim, 296 x 150 mm inside at the rim, its walls drawn in 14.5 mm a side to a 267 x 121 mm floor with an 8 mm round where they meet it, 65 mm deep, 3 mm walls and floor, 0.31 kg (Cambro 32CW135), loose on the counter, centred at (40, 2) with its long side along x. (2) Its flat lift-off cover, 325 x 176 x 3 mm, seated on the rim with a 6 mm deep skirt 1.5 mm clear of the walls and, at its centre, two moulded finger wells (68 mm along x, 39 mm across, 15 mm deep) with a 15 mm land between them, 0.22 kg (Vollrath 31300). (3) Two round egg patties, each a Papetti's 3 1/2 in round fully cooked scrambled egg patty, 1.5 oz (Michael Foods): 89 mm across, 9 mm thick with 3 mm rounded edges, 42.5 g, on the pan's flat floor at its far end, centres at (38.7, 2) and (47.9, 2); 68 mm of flat floor is free at the near end. (4) A solid stainless offset turner: blade 127 mm long (tip to back) and 102 mm wide, 2.5 mm thick, bevelled to 0.6 mm at the tip; a 130 x 22 x 14 mm handle 65 mm above the blade and 30 mm behind it; 0.34 kg (Mercer M18480). It lies on the counter on its blade's back edge and its handle's end (tip up about 20 degrees), blade centre at (50, -16), tip toward +x. (5) A toasted English muffin half (Thomas' Original English Muffins, 13 oz for 6), 95 mm across and 22 mm high, 30 g, on an open sandwich wrapper (18 x 18 cm) centred at (36, -30). Two YAM arms with parallel grippers.
scoring: Scored on the end state; three failures void the run (0) whenever they happen. 0.3: the egg patty rests on the turner's blade (its centre within 10 mm of the blade's outline and within 4 mm of the height of a patty lying flat on the blade's face), its centre carried 2 cm or more past the pan's 325 x 176 mm outline (real trial: the overhead phone camera over a tape line on the counter 2 cm outside the pan). 0.6: the patty rests on the muffin heel, flat within 10 degrees, its centre within 12 mm of the heel's (real trial: overhead phone camera over a printed centre mark), having gone from the pan to the blade to the heel (a patty that leaves the pan other than resting on the blade, skips the blade, is off all three for more than 0.5 s, rises more than 4 mm after leaving the blade, or slides off the blade with its lowest point more than 20 mm above the heel's top (real trial: a side phone camera at counter height filming a vertical ruler tape), such as carried in the fingers, pushed or dropped, scores 0). 1.0: that, and the cover seated back on the pan (within 2 mm in height, centre within 8 mm, tilted under 1 degree; real trial: a 2 mm feeler gauge along the rim) with the other patty still inside. Void: the patty comes out of the pan while the cover is on the pan or resting on it; the cover is clear when its lowest point (plate corner or well bottom) is 10 mm or more above the rim, wherever it is held, or when all of it is off the pan's outline, held or set down flat on the counter; a patty touches the counter outside the pan; the other patty leaves the pan.
reset_notes: Nothing is random: every item starts at its mark.
fidelity: Rigid bodies on GPU at 20 Hz. Patties: 89 mm, 42.5 g (maker's 3 1/2 in, 1.5 oz), 7 to 9 mm thick from mass and density; both thicknesses and a bending patty (27 kPa, 20 mm sag half over a ruler) score 1.0. Patty friction on steel 0.20 to 0.50 and on the heel 0.35 to 1.0, by tilt tests; 1.0 at each end. Pan walls drawn in 14.5 mm a side, the most its 2.37 L capacity allows. Cover 0.22 kg and pan 0.31 kg from makers; turner at its 0.34 kg shipping weight.
scores: Demo: 1.0 (scripted, 716 steps). Cover on the counter, friction ends, 12 or 20 mm wells, 7 mm or bending patty: 1.0 each. Lazy: nothing, fingers pinch out or onto the blade, 1 cm past the outline, slid off beside the heel, dropped from 10 cm, cover slid: 0.0; cover left off 0.6. Dream-1: 0.0.
